nodes.title: Inbound calls, control-plane half (must-be brief 8): inbound.route.set (policy) binds a workspace number to a published agent version, optionally with that agent's inbound deployment whose split then picks the version per call (stable by carrier call id); inbound.route.clear (policy) and inbound.route.list (read); the Numbers page says which agent answers each number and asks for the change. POST /hooks/telephony/inbound (signed with VP_TELEPHONY_WEBHOOK_SECRET, like the KYC hook) finds the workspace by the called number, looks the caller up in that workspace only (tombstone, erased contact, workspace suppression, contact), holds money against the wallet and the workspace cap only (never a campaign cap; G9's rule for the amount), opens an inbound conversation with no attempt, mints a ticket (direction inbound, consent basis inbound, transport sip_inbound, attemptId null, inbound {who, noMarketing, calledNumber}) and returns the runtime's stream URL. Refusals are plain words with a code: not_our_number (404), not_answering (409, unbound or no published version), number_paused (409), ambiguous_number (409), wallet_low / cap_reached (402), runtime_unavailable (503). A carrier retry of the same call id returns the same conversation (telephony_event 'inbound:'+callId, and a unique carrier_call_id per workspace)
nodes.rationale: They called us: a caller who opted out or asked to be erased still reaches the agent, with no memory and marked no-marketing on the ticket; an erased caller gets no facts, no name and their number is not stored on the call; an opted-out caller keeps service facts. An unknown caller gets nothing of anyone's, including another workspace's contact with the same number. The hold settles at call.ended by its conversation (reservation.conversation_id). The call log and the call page say Inbound. Built against the fake runtime and FakeTelephony; the voice runtime wires sip_inbound later.
nodes.reverse_if: The owner wants inbound answered even with an empty wallet (then answer and bill afterwards), or a duty-hours rule for inbound lines.

nodes.title: Inbound's other halves: the voice runtime answers a sip_inbound ticket on the stream it returns (and honours inbound.noMarketing), and the carrier relay (Plivo answer URL) calls /hooks/telephony/inbound and connects the leg; both wait on voice and the campaigns go. Concurrency: the dial gate already holds back 20% of lines for inbound, but the inbound hook does not yet count live calls against the workspace's line limit.

events.details: tests/inbound.test.ts (6): binding (policy, approved; a candidate and another workspace's number refused), unbound and unknown numbers refused in words with no ticket or hold, a forged signature 401, a known caller gets their facts and an inbound ticket with a wallet-only hold and the stream back, a carrier retry is the same call, the hold settles at call.ended and call.search says inbound, an erased caller gets no memory, facts, name or stored number, an opted-out caller no memory and no marketing, another workspace's contact is never read, an empty wallet refuses in words. Browser flow: the Numbers page shows the binding (screenshot product/web/shots/numbers-inbound.png); the a11y and copy flows pass.
